p: Timing is everything round here. On a big event day, Olympic Way turns into a sea of shirts, flags and fans, and the whole Wembley Park area gets very busy indeed. If you want a relaxed hit in the nets, an off-peak afternoon or a quieter weeknight will feel very different to the hour before kick-off. If you're heading here specifically for the atmosphere, though, booking a session around a match or gig is a cracking way to get in the mood.

Getting here is easy without a car. Wembley Park station is on the Jubilee and Metropolitan lines and sits at the top of Olympic Way, while Wembley Stadium station has trains from Marylebone. Expect queues for the trains after big events, so either leave a bit early or build in time to hang around BOXPARK while the crowds thin out.

Beyond the stadium, the area has plenty more going on. OVO Arena Wembley hosts concerts and shows just next door, and the London Designer Outlet is a few minutes' walk away with shops, restaurants and a cinema. There's also a fair bit of public space and public art scattered around Wembley Park, which is pleasant for a stroll on a dry day. With so much in walking distance, you can easily turn a quick hour at the nets into a whole afternoon or evening out.
